rows.name: Compose — Revise Document
rows.toolDescription: Revise the WHOLE document currently open in Compose. Use when the user asks to revise, review, align, or flag risks across the ENTIRE document they have open (e.g. 'align this whole contract with our playbook', 'flag any risky clauses in this document', 'clean up the clarity of this agreement', 'revise this document to tighten the indemnification language'). This is DIFFERENT from compose-draft-alternative (which rewrites only the ONE clause the user has selected/highlighted) and compose-draft-document (which drafts a BRAND-NEW document from scratch) — use this capability when the user wants an existing OPEN document reviewed or revised end-to-end. Produces pending track-change edits and/or anchored review comments the attorney accepts, replaces, resolves, or undoes; it does NOT persist any change until accepted. Required arg: revisionIntent (one of align-clauses, flag-risks, improve-clarity, custom — infer from the user's phrasing; default to improve-clarity if unclear). Optional arg: instruction (free-text refinement, required for custom).

rows.name: create-matter (default)
rows.toolDescription: Create a new matter (a Spaarke sprk_matter record) from this conversation. Use when the user asks to create, open, start, or intake a matter, or says something like 'create a matter from this file, practice area <label>, type <label>'. This capability DRAFTS the proposed matter (name, description, practice-area/matter-type LABEL suggestions, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record. After presenting the proposal to the user, create the record by calling dataverse.create_record with tablename 'sprk_matter' and an item carrying: sprk_mattername (the proposal's matter name, or the user's stated name if they gave one), sprk_matterdescription (the proposal description PLUS a final provenance line that MUST name the source document file, e.g. 'Provenance: source document nda-acme.pdf' — copy file names VERBATIM from the session context). PRACTICE AREA / MATTER TYPE RULE: sprk_practicearea and sprk_mattertype are LOOKUPS to sprk_practicearea_ref / sprk_mattertype_ref (never multi-select choices, never free text) — before asking the user to confirm, resolve the practice-area/matter-type LABEL (from the proposal's suggestions or the user's own words) to its reference-row GUID via dataverse.read_query IN THE SAME TURN, and set {"relatedTable":"sprk_practicearea_ref","recordId":"guid"} (same pattern for sprk_mattertype_ref); if you cannot resolve a confident match, OMIT that column and mention the intended value inside sprk_matterdescription instead — never guess a GUID and never use '@odata.bind'. Records you create belong to the calling user automatically. POST-CONFIRMATION RULE: ask for confirmation in chat AT MOST ONCE — presenting the drafted proposal and asking once is the ONLY chat question allowed. The moment the user affirms the proposal ('yes', 'create it', 'confirm'), IMMEDIATELY invoke dataverse.create_record with the sprk_matter contract above IN THAT SAME TURN — do NOT announce that you are about to proceed and ask again, do NOT re-invoke this capability to regenerate the draft. The CONFIRMATION DIALOG presented by dataverse.create_record is the approval step: invoke the write tool and let it suspend.

rows.name: create-task (default)
rows.toolDescription: Create a follow-up task (a Spaarke To Do / action item) from this conversation. Use when the user asks to create a task, to-do, follow-up, action item, or reminder about the session's documents, analyses, or findings (e.g. 'create a follow-up task to send this by Friday'). Requires a due date and an assignee — supply them from the conversation; if either is missing they will be elicited. RELATIVE DATE RULE: resolve relative due dates ('tomorrow', 'next Friday', 'in two weeks') against the current date given in the '## Current Date' context block — never guess the year — and state the resolved absolute date in the proposal. This capability DRAFTS the proposed task (title, description, priority suggestion, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record. After presenting the proposal to the user, create the record by calling dataverse.create_record with tablename 'sprk_event' and an item carrying: sprk_eventname (the proposal title), sprk_description (the proposal description PLUS a final provenance line that MUST name the source document file and the source analysis ledger key, e.g. 'Provenance: source document nda-acme.pdf; source analysis 651194cd-3670-f111-ab0e-70a8a590c51c@t3' — copy ledger keys VERBATIM from the '## Session Outputs (stored ledger)' context block), sprk_duedate (the resolved due date as yyyy-MM-dd), and sprk_eventtype_ref as a lookup {"relatedTable":"sprk_eventtype_ref","name":"Task","recordId":"124f5fc9-98ff-f011-8406-7c1e525abd8b"}. ASSIGNEE RULE: the assignee column is sprk_assignedto1 (a lookup to the contact table — recordId GUID REQUIRED). When the user names SOMEONE ELSE, resolve that person's contact GUID via dataverse.search_data or dataverse.read_query FIRST and set sprk_assignedto1; NEVER pass a lookup object without recordId — it will be rejected. When the task is for the requesting user themselves ('assign to me'): the record already belongs to them automatically; try to resolve THEIR contact record by their name/email if it appears in the conversation and set sprk_assignedto1 with the resolved GUID — if you cannot resolve it, OMIT the column and state the assignee's name inside sprk_description instead. REGARDING RULE: when this chat is hosted on a record (see the 'Context: This chat is hosted on…' line), also set the matching regarding lookup with the HOST record's id — sprk_regardingmatter for a matter, sprk_regardingproject for a project, sprk_regardinginvoice for an invoice, sprk_regardingaccount for an account, sprk_regardingcontact for a contact (e.g. {"relatedTable":"sprk_matter","recordId":"<host record id>"}). That write is confirmation-gated: it suspends for the user's explicit approval before executing, and after approval the created record's id and link are reported back in chat. POST-CONFIRMATION RULE: ask for confirmation in chat AT MOST ONCE — presenting the drafted proposal and asking once is the ONLY chat question allowed. The moment the user affirms the proposal ('yes', 'create it', 'confirm'), IMMEDIATELY invoke dataverse.create_record with the sprk_event contract above IN THAT SAME TURN — do NOT announce that you are about to proceed and ask again, do NOT re-invoke this capability to regenerate the draft. The CONFIRMATION DIALOG presented by dataverse.create_record is the approval step: invoke the write tool and let it suspend.

rows.name: Honest Refusal (no_match_handler)
rows.toolDescription: REFUSAL — call this when the user's request matches no other available capability or tool and cannot be answered from the session's documents or connected records with citations. Renders the platform's honest statement of what it can and cannot do; relay its returned message verbatim. Required arg: unsupported_request — a short neutral label (10 words or fewer) of what the user asked for (e.g. 'document translation'); do not copy the user's message verbatim. Terminal informational output — no side effects, never suspends.
